title: Learning robust medical image segmentation from multi-source annotations (UMA-Net)
mechanism: Pixel-level annotation-uncertainty estimates weight the loss, and an image-level quality module routes each sample to a high-quality or a low-quality decoder head.
adaptation: Image quality is set from source and label-width deviation: BMRK, SDLE and the speck-level H36 labels go to the low-quality head. Pixel weights come from 5-seed disagreement. The high-quality head is used at test.
min_experiment: Arm: two-head routing by source quality, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: BMRK crack and inactive IoU, overall crack IoU. Kill if the BMRK crack IoU gain is below 0.03.
evidence: R (web abstract): on simulated JSRT lung data, +5.31% over single-annotation noise-robust methods and +1.47% over multi-source methods; tested on chest X-ray, fundus and breast DCE-MRI.
